name: d1-2B
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B (config.json max_position_embeddings 128000). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Same tri-hybrid LFM3 text stack as LFM3-1.7B: 13 gated short-convolution layers (conv), 5 sliding-window attention layers (sliding_window 256), 6 full-attention layers at indices 2,6,10,14,18,22; GQA 16 heads / 4 KV heads, head_dim 128. Vision encoder is separate: 14 layers = 8 gated depthwise 2D convolutions interleaved with 6 bidirectional full-attention layers, 16x16 patches, spatial_merge_size 2 (each 2x2 patch block becomes one language token).
notes: ADDED 2026-11-01 from the trending feed (trendingScore 130, the top-ranked uncovered decision model of the sweep). A DECISION model (task=decision), not a text generator: it takes a state (text or JSON) plus pictures or video and a schema of typed questions (noul, choice, multi-choice, score, text, number, date, box, boxes) and returns a probability per option from ONE forward pass with zero output tokens. Post-trained from LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B, which the catalog already holds (models/lfm3-vl-2b), so this record inherits the base's config: 24 text layers, tri-hybrid 13 conv / 5 sliding-window (256) / 6 full attention, hidden 2048, 16 query / 4 KV heads, head_dim 128. CONFIG CHECK: the repo's own config.json carries d1_* keys (d1_codes 2, d1_attention 'set', d1_set_size 16, d1_numbers true, d1_vision_max_pixels 1638400) on top of the lfm3_vl model_type, which is what makes it a decision readout rather than a next-token head - it is not a rename of the base. PARAMS: HF safetensors total 1,918,181,888 = 1.918B, identical to the base's tensor count (the readout reuses the existing head), and the card states 1.92B, so params_b is the API count and active_params_b is the whole model (dense). HARDWARE GATE: passes easily - 1.918B active, ~1 GiB at 4-bit against a 128 GiB budget, 24 layers, and 5.7 ms per decision on an H100 PCIe / 3.8 ms on an MI325X per the card's own speed table (median of 20 warm calls after model.compile(), bf16). KV: recorded 0 on the same basis as models/lfm3-vl-2b - every attention layer sits behind a 256-token sliding window or a constant-state conv layer, so nothing grows per token. The six full-attention layers would cost 6 x 2 x 4 KV heads x 128 head_dim x 2 B = 12,288 B/token if they held an unbounded cache, which they do not. flops_per_token_active = 2 x 1.918e9 = 3.836e9, the schema's one-pass approximation and identical to the base's value; it excludes the vision encoder per image, which is a prefill-shaped cost, not a per-token one. WHAT IT BEATS: on the card's own single table, which scores d1-2B, d1-3B, d1-Omni-2B and d1-omni-600M on the same items with the same scoring, d1-2B leads d1-3B at UNDER TWO THIRDS the parameters on 5 of 7 decision rows - DecisionBench Hanno v1 77.1 vs 73.1, DecisionBench.ai v4 85.2 vs 83.6, JevBench v1.4.1 77.9 vs 76.2, the public suite 51.1 vs 49.0, and the card's own board 63.2 vs 58.8 - and it leads the whole family on the 19-benchmark vision average (70.2 vs 65.4 for d1-3B, 67.7 for d1-Omni-2B), including VisWebBench 96.2 vs 71.4 and ImajevBench 75.5 vs 64.0. That is the upset: a 2B decision model beating its own 3B sibling on five of seven decision tests. WHAT IT LOSES: Fast Decisions 58.8 vs d1-3B's 59.3, and Typed Decisions 61.3 vs 65.0 for d1-3B and 63.1 for d1-Omni-2B - the typed-extraction slice is where the extra capacity still pays. It also trails d1-Omni-2B on POPE (88.7 vs 89.9) and V* (76.4 tie). NOT BOARD-VALIDATED: the card's 51.1 is the PUBLIC suite on edition v0.3, and the board's data/index.json read 2026-10-29T14:04:16Z has NO row for d1-2b at all (it lists only d1-3b at full score 31.12 and d1-omni-600m at 11.75), so nothing here is self-reported-but-checked or board-measured; it is the vendor's own run and every benchmark row is marked vendor_claim. The card's 'Our board (over a hundred public and private benchmarks)' 63.2 is Liquid's internal aggregate, NOT the community Decision Index, and must never be filed in data/decision_index.jsonl. Three of the vision rows (POPE, MME, VisualWebBench) are called saturated by the card itself. LICENCE: LFM Open License v1.0 (tag 'other'), repo created 2026-10-24. COMPARISON TO THE CATALOG'S OTHER DECISION MODELS: on the board's 0.4.1 scale the best 4B-class decision models sit at 43-47 (jpt-4b 43.04, decider-35b-a3b's NVFP4 47.11), and d1-3B is 31.12, so if Liquid's 51.1 v0.3 reading survives a board rescore d1-2B would be the strongest sub-3B decision model in the catalog. It has NOT been rescore, so this record claims only the card's table.

This is the PUBLIC suite on the card's v0.3 edition, NOT the current 0.4.1 board: d1-2B has no row in the board's data/index.json (generated 2026-10-29T14:04:16Z, suite decision-index-0.3), which lists only d1-3b and d1-omni-600m from LiquidAI, so the number is not board-validated and the two edits must not be subtracted from each other. Harness: model.system_one, one forward pass per request.
